release_notes:
Release v1.2.2 - 2026-11-19

📚 Documentation:
  • docs: review fixes in five languages: region check text and note, Cost Explorer bound (a fortieth, at least 5 s), a hung listing keeps the process alive, cache subnet group read failure keeps the sheet [skip release]
  • docs: network guide counts ElastiCache clusters and RDS DB instances and not DB subnet groups; legacy uploads bound to the named bucket; exit 5 row, in five languages [skip release]
  • docs: sample blocks regenerated (Cost Explorer line, no 'No output format specified'); troubleshooting and run-a-scan: unknown region, slow Cost Explorer, Ctrl-C and SIGTERM lines, detail-call and state notes, nothing to upload, --resume console, default-run line, in five languages [skip release]
  • docs: status page for the second patch: Cost Explorer warning, snapshot note, nothing to upload, misspelled region, Ctrl-C and SIGTERM removed; new limits (Cost Explorer bound, process after deadline, RDS cluster, consolidated report session), in five languages [skip release]
  • docs: template field reference regenerated (five corrected descriptions); with --template one failed format does not stop the other, in five languages [skip release]
  • docs: move the v1.2.1 notes out of Unreleased in the changelog
  • docs: archive documentation versions after release v1.2.1 [skip release]

♻️ Code Refactoring:
  • refactor: the generator reads the detail-call ledger source from discovery's DETAIL_SOURCE instead of its own copy of the string (behaviour identical, tests untouched)

✅ Tests:
  • tests: the quoted region texts of the troubleshooting page equal the code's (region check wording and run note)
  • tests: the claims tests assert the patched behaviour the pages state (snapshot note, nothing to upload with and without --fail-if-empty, first account's session for the consolidated report, quoted messages equal the code's)
  • tests: the slow Cost Explorer pair counts discovery's warning records instead of reading the console stream, which a handler left by an earlier test can bypass in a full run
  • tests/regression: row K1 moves the Ctrl-C message that fix2/track-c prints into current; the exit code stays 1
  • tests: the cross-track pairs of the second patch run with both sides on the branch; a slow Cost Explorer gives one warning that agrees with the run note (fails today: two lines that blame the network)

📝 Other Changes:
  • changelog: the second patch states every change a v1.2.1 user can notice (review L3) and the review fixes (account-bound ElastiCache counts, Network sheet kept, modes of re-saved files, unknown regions tried, Cost Explorer floor, --audit-output on a symlink or pipe)
  • L2: --audit-output on a symlink, a named pipe or another non-regular file is written as in v1.2.1
  • L2: test: --audit-output on a symlink exits 1 and leaves the link; a named pipe receives the JSON (fails today)
  • M3: the Cost Explorer bound under a short account limit has a 5 s floor per step
  • M3: test: a Cost Explorer answer of 3 s is read under a 60 s account limit, and the bound has a floor (fails today)
  • M2: a region the installed botocore does not know is tried as in v1.2.1; only a failed one is named, with both causes
  • M2: test: a region the installed botocore does not know is still tried, and a failed one is named with both causes (fails today)
  • M1: re-saving a configuration, template, checker text report or tag compliance JSON keeps the existing file's mode
  • M1: test: re-saving a configuration, template, checker text report or tag compliance JSON keeps the existing file's mode (fails today)
  • H2: any failure to read the cache subnet groups leaves the Network Analysis sheet as without ElastiCache counts, with one warning and a run note
  • H2: test: a report that runs its own network analysis keeps the sheet and gets the note when the ElastiCache endpoint is unreachable (fails today)
  • H2: test: an unreachable ElastiCache endpoint keeps the Network Analysis sheet, with one warning and a run note (fails today)
  • H1: an ElastiCache cluster is counted only through a cache subnet group of its own account
  • H1: test: a cluster of another account is not counted in the first account's VPC through a cache subnet group of the same name (fails today)
